propositions: git fetch hangs intermittently on byte-starved connections because curl handle lacks throughput-keyed abort, bounded only by 300s wall-clock timeout instead of per-second transfer rate
fetch stall causes reviews to defer or fail after burning full 300s timeout budget when connection accepts but sends zero bytes
adding http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime git config parameters enables abort on throughput threshold rather than wall time, allowing stall detection in ~10 seconds
in-process retry of low-speed abort failures allows transient stalls to self-heal within the same review instead of deferring to backfill pass
code refactoring moves git subprocess and fetch-locking cluster from repo_snapshot.py into new git_fetch.py module to satisfy 800 LOC module-size cap
solution preserves legitimate slow-but-progressing fetches (tested at 2000-4000 B/s sustained throughput) while aborting true stalls
